title: Cohen rings exist
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. Then there exist a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] (a discrete valuation ring whose maximal ideal is $p\Lambda$ and which is $p\Lambda$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]) and a ring isomorphism $\Lambda/p\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328 (lemma-cohen-rings-exist, line 44878) and its proof (lines 44885-44910); Cohen ring: Definition Tag 0327 (definition-cohen-ring, line 44872)

proof.text: Map the residue field of the p-adic integers to k by PadicInt.residueField followed by ZMod.castHom.

Apply IsLocalRing.exists_flat_local_extension_given_residue_field to obtain S, its flat map from Z_p, its maximal ideal identity, and a residue field equivalence. Mapping the principal ideal (p) proves maximalIdeal S = (p).
Construct Lambda = AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal S) S, and apply adicCompletion_dvr_of_flat_padicInt to this fixed construction for its domain and DVR properties.

The maximal ideal of S is generated by p and is therefore finitely generated. AdicCompletion.maximalIdeal_eq_map_of_fg and isAdicComplete_self identify the maximal ideal of Lambda as (p) and give (p)-adic completeness. These are the finitely generated versions in Mathlib, so S need not be Noetherian; locality follows from the field quotient and the Jacobson-radical property of completeness.

AdicCompletion.ker_evalOneₐ_eq_map and evalOneₐ_surjective show evaluation Lambda -> S/(p) is surjective with kernel (p). Apply Ideal.quotEquivOfEq and RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective; compose with the residue equivalence S/maximalIdeal S -> k from step 2.
Package hp, the domain and DVR properties, the maximal-ideal identity, completeness and the quotient equivalence into the unchanged conclusion using IsCohenRing.
